extras.quota_verbatim: Free plan: unlimited projects and unlimited publishes; each project capped at 450 MB and 10,100 files. No account-level byte quota.
extras.limits_verbatim: 450 MB and 10,100 files per project (hard: 'Aborted - Unable to publish. Application too large'); no bandwidth figure published; no per-file cap documented but it inherits the project cap. Re-publishing replaces the whole project (full-sync deploy), so appending one file re-uploads the directory.
extras.egress_verbatim: No bandwidth quota or metering is documented anywhere on the free plan; every project is served from all 10 of Surge's own edge nodes ('Every project—free or paid—serves from all of them').
extras.chaining_verbatim: Unlimited projects x 450 MB = arbitrary total per account; unlimited free accounts (email+password in-terminal, no card). 20 TiB archive = ~45,500 projects of 450 MB. Sharding is natural because each project is just a folder.
extras.tooling_verbatim: Official `surge` CLI (npm, ~free) and a documented raw REST deploy API: PUT /:domain with Basic auth, Content-Type: application/gzip, a gzipped tarball body plus file-count and project-size headers. That is directly scriptable, no CLI needed.
extras.agent_focus: Static/docs/wiki hosts with big free limits: GitHub Pages, GitLab Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, Vercel, Surge, Neocities, ReadTheDocs, GitBook, Notion, Outline, Confluence free, MkDocs hosts, per-site caps

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
